description:
Look a word up in the real Livonian–Estonian–Latvian dictionary and return only
attested content, so translations are grounded, not invented.

Search a meaning (in English/Latvian/Estonian) to find the Livonian headword, or a
Livonian word to confirm it exists and read its sense, part of speech and examples.
See the `query` and `search_language` parameter docs for how to phrase a query. By
default each match's full inflection table is returned inline, so one call usually
suffices; on a broad query only the first N tables expand (the rest are listed as
handles to fetch with livonian_get_inflections). Returns Markdown plus the same result as
structuredContent matching the declared outputSchema.

Results are cached server-side, so repeating a query is instant and free; a
first-time query reaches the live dictionary and calls are rate limited — on a
rate-limit error, wait a few seconds and retry instead of re-issuing immediately.
Dictionary content is from livonian.tech (CC BY-SA 4.0 — attribute if republished).

SearchLanguage.description:
Which language the query word is matched against. Headwords come back in
Livonian and glosses in English either way; this only selects the language the
query term is in. Codes are the site's own.
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

include_forms.description: When true (default), each match's full inflection table is returned INLINE — usable cases/tenses in ONE call, no follow-up livonian_get_inflections. Set false to get just the headword handles + glosses: a cheap way to SCREEN several candidate words or synonyms (which exist? which sense?) before spending forms on the one you pick. Bounded by a per-search cap — use max_forms to raise or lower it for this call.
include_forms.title: Include Forms

max_forms.description: Optional override for how many inflection tables to expand this call (0–12). Raise it to pull more tables in ONE call on a broad query, or set a small value to keep a broad query cheap. On an uncached query each table is fetched sequentially with polite pacing toward the upstream, so a high value on a cold broad query is slow — the bound limits upstream fan-out, not just response size. Omit to use the server's default cap.
max_forms.title: Max Forms

query.description: A SINGLE content word, not a phrase. Exactly one word per call — even with several candidates or synonyms in mind, search them one at a time ('see', then 'look'), never combined into one query like 'see look'. Drop function words and infinitive markers — search 'to water' as 'water', 'the sea' as 'sea'. The dictionary matches one attested headword, so a multi-word query often returns nothing even when the word exists; search the main word first, then refine. May be Livonian, Latvian, Estonian, or English (e.g. 'jarā', 'away', 'sea'). Matching is bidirectional. An inflected Livonian form (search_language='liv') is resolved to its dictionary lemma automatically when the form is known — the result says so when that happened.
query.title: Query

search_language.description: Language your query word is in — selects which language the search matches against: 'eng' (default), 'liv', 'lat', or 'est'. For English→Livonian translation, keep 'eng'. Glosses are in English.

name: livonian_search

Entry.description:
One dictionary entry (one upstream result card): the headword with its
pronunciation, part of speech, paradigm anchors, and senses.

``entry_id`` + ``word_class`` are the same anchors carried by an
:class:`InflectionHandle` — feed them to ``livonian_get_inflections`` for the full paradigm.
Every field except ``headword``/``gloss`` defaults, so a card missing a
pronunciation, type code, or senses still validates.

entry_id.description: Numeric word id for the forms endpoint.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

Entry.title: Entry

Example.description:
One usage example for a sense: the Livonian sentence and its English translation.
``english`` is empty when the upstream entry gives the Livonian without a gloss.
Example.title: Example

InflectionHandle.description:
A reliable, structured anchor for fetching a full paradigm. Feed
``entry_id`` + ``word_class`` to ``livonian_get_inflections`` — or ask ``search`` to
include the table inline (``forms``).

entry_id.description: Numeric word id used by the forms endpoint.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

forms.description: The full inflection paradigm, populated when a search is asked to include forms. None when not requested or beyond the cap; category 'none' when the word has no paradigm.
forms.title: Forms

InflectionHandle.title: InflectionHandle

NominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/numeral/pronoun: case → {singular, plural}.

``category`` discriminates this from the verbal and not-found shapes — switch on it
before reading the body.

cases.description: Case name (English, lower-case) → its singular/plural forms, in paradigm order, e.g. 'nominative', 'genitive', 'partitive'.
cases.title: Cases

source.default: Ernštreits, Valts (ed. in chief), Viitso, Tiit-Rein, Kurpniece, Milda & Vāvere, Signis. 2024. Livonian morphology database. Riga: University of Latvia Livonian Institute. https://livonian.tech/ (CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) Adapted: reformatted and condensed from the original.
source.title: Source

NominalParadigm.title: NominalParadigm

NumberForms.description: A nominal cell: the two number forms of one case. Livonian forms are verbatim.
NumberForms.title: NumberForms

ParadigmNotFound.description:
No paradigm for this entry_id/word_class (the morphology DB has none, or the
handle was wrong). ``found`` is False and there is no table body.

source.default: Ernštreits, Valts (ed. in chief), Viitso, Tiit-Rein, Kurpniece, Milda & Vāvere, Signis. 2024. Livonian morphology database. Riga: University of Latvia Livonian Institute. https://livonian.tech/ (CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) Adapted: reformatted and condensed from the original.
source.title: Source

ParadigmNotFound.title: ParadigmNotFound

Polarity.description:
A verbal cell: the two polarities of one person in one mood/tense. ``negative``
is the ready-to-use form — the negation auxiliary (äb/äd/iz/algõ…) is already folded
in (e.g. ``äb toup``), not orphaned in a separate column. Livonian forms are verbatim.
Polarity.title: Polarity

SearchLanguage.description:
Which language the query word is matched against. Headwords come back in
Livonian and glosses in English either way; this only selects the language the
query term is in. Codes are the site's own.
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

Sense.description:
One sense of a headword: its gloss and any usage examples. ``label`` is the
upstream sense marker (``a)``, ``b)``) and is empty for a single, unlabelled sense.
Sense.title: Sense

VerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way the grammar is: finite moods/tenses by
person and polarity, plus the non-finite forms.

``category`` discriminates this from the nominal and not-found shapes.

finite.description: Mood/tense (English, lower-case: 'present', 'past', 'conditional', …) → pronoun (Livonian, verbatim: ma/sa/ta/mēg/tēg/ne) → {affirmative, negative}. The negative already includes its auxiliary.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite section (English, lower-case: 'principal parts', 'participles') → form label (English) → the Livonian form.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite

forms_truncated.description: How many handles did NOT get an inline table because the per-search cap was reached. Refine the query or call livonian_get_inflections.

resolved_from.description: The original inflected query when search_method='lemma_index'; empty on a direct match.

resolved_lemma.title: Resolved Lemma

search_method.description: How the match was found: 'direct' = the query itself matched; 'lemma_index' = the query was an inflected Livonian form, resolved to its dictionary lemma via the cached paradigm index and re-searched.
